opening.argument: The video presents a reported Starbucks gift-card and birthday-reward exploit as an interview and technical demonstration intended to alert Starbucks, not as a completed fraud scheme. Its stated purpose is corrective: the hackers hope the message reaches Starbucks so the exploit can be fixed, while viewers are expressly told, “And you should never use this card.” The record also distinguishes potential conduct from actual fraud, stating, “These are potential felonies, these are potential frauds, not actual frauds.” No fake accounts were actually created, and the demonstration did not establish completed account creation, reward redemption, actual fraud, viewer payment, or an outcome against Starbucks. Patreon and subscription requests are ordinary audience-support prompts, not conditions for participating in the demonstration.

citations.quote: These hackers hope this message will make it to Starbucks so they can fix this terrible exploit.
And you should never use this card.
These are potential felonies, these are potential frauds, not actual frauds.
No fake accounts were actually created in this demonstration.
